title: FidelityAttestation
description: DRAFT 2026-06-10. The justified-verdict substrate (detection_verdict.schema.json) applied to A RULE ITSELF instead of an event. A FidelityAttestation is a content-addressed, reproducible, queryable claim about what a specific detection rule COVERS and what it structurally CANNOT, grounded on a named corpus. The canon-novel artifact of the detection inversion: Sigma/CAR carry only free-text 'falsepositives:' + human tags; this is a MACHINE-CHECKABLE, provenance-backed fidelity record that travels with the rule. THE LOAD-BEARING DISCIPLINE (made structural by the 2026-06-07 LSASS correction): the claim is ALWAYS scoped 'rule R, on corpus C, w.r.t. technique T' and NEVER universal ('Sigma misses T'). Generated without corpus-grounding + reproducible evidence + honest scope it is just opinion-with-a-hash; the schema forces all three. STIX/TAXII is the distribution binding (a custom SDO via extension-definition with an SRO to the attack-pattern), NOT the source of truth — this contract is. See ../design/self_validation_architecture.md, detection_verdict.schema.json, carrier.md, cid.md, guarantee_certificate.schema.json.

belnap.description: A carrier.md Belnap Four value as a string. none=(0,0) no info; true=(1,0); false=(0,1); both=(1,1) contradiction. NOT a bare bool — 'we did not evaluate this rule on this corpus' is 'none', never 'false' (absence of evidence != evidence of absence).

cid.description: A content address per cid.md (a node's recipe CID = its prov:Entity id). Justification is reachable by walking the provenance DAG from this id.

rule.description: Identity of the SPECIFIC rule evaluated — pinned to exact bytes. A rule is a moving target (SigmaHQ is a git repo); binding the attestation to a content address makes it reproducible and prevents 'this rule' from silently meaning a later, fixed version.

id.description: rule identifier — Sigma rule id / CAR analytic id / title.

source.description: provenance of the rule text: 'SigmaHQ', 'MITRE CAR', a local path. Source-trust feeds the evaluation tier (a vendored snapshot vs upstream HEAD).

version_cid.description: CID of the EXACT rule text evaluated (one-hash-three-roles). The attestation is about this version and no other; a fixed rule gets a new CID and a new attestation.

corpus.description: Identity of the dataset R was evaluated on — THE honest-scope binding. Every coverage claim is conditional on this corpus; the schema makes 'on corpus C' un-droppable.

cid.description: content address of the corpus (or the specific dataset file evaluated).

event_count.description: OPTIONAL scale context. Coverage measured on a tiny corpus is weak evidence (the n~=11 finite-sample floor); carry the scale so a reader weights the claim honestly.

technique.description: ATT&CK id (e.g. T1003.001) — the hypothesis the rule is measured against, itself a validatable label, never the bedrock.

coverage.description: Did R catch T on C? true=R fired on the ground-truth instances of T in C (caught). false=R MISSED ground-truth instances AND the ground truth is known (T occurred, R was silent). none=not evaluated, or ground truth unknown — a 'none' is NOT a faked 'false' ('we didn't establish ground truth' != 'R missed'). both=contradictory (fired on some instances, missed others; or two evaluations disagree — a soundness alarm).

cause.description: WHY it missed — structured, not free text. REQUIRED when coverage in {false, both}. Distinguishes a real rule flaw (allowlist/coarse-proxy/logic-gap) from an OBSERVABILITY limit (missing-telemetry), which is honestly NONE-shaped, not a fault of the rule.

kind.description: allowlist=an FP-reduction filter waved the attack through (e.g. a path allowlist a LOLBin runs as). coarse-proxy=the rule's predicate is a loose proxy for the true mechanism (e.g. GrantedAccess|endswith '10' vs bitwise &0x10). logic-gap=the condition genuinely does not cover the procedure. missing-telemetry=the required data-component is absent → the technique is UNOBSERVABLE in C → this is NONE-shaped (not a rule flaw); a 'missing-telemetry' cause should pair with coverage='none', not 'false'. other=specify in detail.

detail.description: the specifics — e.g. 'filter_generic allowlists C:\Windows\system32\; comsvcs MiniDump abuses rundll32, a trusted signed system32 LOLBin, so the attack runs AS the allowlisted path'.

locus.description: OPTIONAL — the exact rule element responsible: 'filter_generic', 'GrantedAccess|endswith'. Localizes the flaw for an upstream fix/PR.

evidence.description: The reproducible artifact that DEMONSTRATES the coverage verdict — not opinion. REQUIRED when coverage in {false, both}. Without a CID-addressed, re-runnable evidence node this is opinion-with-a-hash; the schema forbids that for a non-trivial verdict.

method.description: how the verdict was established — e.g. 'allowlist-off exact-mechanism (GrantedAccess & 0x10) re-evaluation flagged the reader R suppressed'.

flagged.description: what the corrected check caught that R suppressed — e.g. ['rundll32.exe comsvcs MiniDump on lsass, 1 event']. The concrete miss, carried.

cid.description: content address of the evidence run (the experiment's output node) — reproducible: same corpus CID + same method → same evidence CID.

scope.description: The honest-scoping GUARD — the explicit boundary that prevents over-generalization. Made a REQUIRED, structural field by the 2026-06-07 LSASS correction (the cell over-claimed 'off-the-shelf Sigma misses comsvcs'; a dedicated SigmaHQ rule catches it via CallTrace — the cell had tested only one generic rule and never parsed CallTrace). The attestation is a RULE-COVERAGE measurement, not a 'the framework is blind' claim.

claim.description: the precisely-scoped claim, always of the form 'rule R (version_cid), on corpus C (cid), w.r.t. technique T'. Never universal.

not_claimed.description: explicit NEGATIVE scope — what this attestation does NOT assert. E.g. 'does NOT claim SigmaHQ misses T1003.001 — proc_creation_win_lolbin_comsvcs (CallTrace) catches comsvcs; only the generic process_access rule tested here was evaluated.'

rules_not_evaluated.description: OPTIONAL — named related rules that EXIST but were not tested. The coverage-measurement honesty: we measured ONE rule's coverage, not the rule corpus's. A reader knows the denominator was not exhausted.

evaluation.description: The tier THIS ATTESTATION earned — the guarantee fold applied to the attestation's own epistemic standing (parallel to guarantee_certificate.schema.json, which tiers a detection's numeric rigor; this tiers an attestation's reproducibility). The floor the design note warns against ('opinion-with-a-hash') is the 'asserted' tier.

tier.description: reproducible=corpus-grounded AND the evidence run reproduces from the recorded CIDs (the earned tier). asserted=claimed but not mechanically reproduced (opinion-with-a-hash — honest, but the floor). absent=no evaluation ran (recorded absence, not a silent blank).

custody.description: the corpus's custody at ingest (detection_verdict custody semantics): true=signed+digest-matched, none=unsigned/silent. Test corpora (OTRF/flaws) are custody=none and the attestation says so rather than faking a chain.

provenance.description: CID of this attestation's own provenance DAG node — full justification on demand (rule bytes, corpus, evidence run, all reachable). Justification IS the result, not a side-log.

allOf.$comment: A non-trivial coverage verdict (false/both) must carry both a structured cause and reproducible evidence — the discipline that keeps an attestation from being opinion-with-a-hash.
